newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf advertising rises to $334 million Jan-May 97.
newsitem.headline: Gulf advertising rises to $334 million Jan-May 97.

text.p: Advertising expenditure in six Gulf Arab states between January and May 1997 rose to $334 million from $293 million in the same period in 1996, the Pan Arab Research Centre (PARC) said.
In the first five months of 1995 spending was $256 million.
The figure for 1997 jumps to $474 million if "pan-Arab" media -- which cover other Arab countries in addition to Gulf states -- are included.
This compares to $377 million in 1996 and $315 million in 1995, PARC said in a report received by Reuters on Tuesday.
PARC is a Dubai-based market research institute.

Advertising expenditure by the six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states -- Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain and Qatar -- in the full year 1996 stood at $699 million, up from $595 million in 1995, PARC said.
GCC plus pan-Arab advertising in 1996 stood at $923 million, up from $751 million in 1995, PARC said.

Saudi Arabia, the biggest advertising market in the GCC with 18 million citizens, spent $151 million on advertising in the first five months of 1997, up from $123 million in the same period in 1996 and $114 million in 1995.
The United Arab Emirates, the region's second-largest advertising market, spent $88 million from January to May this year, up from $82 million in 1996 and $65 million in 1995.
Kuwait, which trails in third place, spent $63 million in the five month period this year, increasing from $60 million in the 1996 period and $50 million in the first five months of 1995.
Advertising executives have said that the industry is still in its infancy in the Gulf, and there are few sustained media campaigns to build brand recognition and product loyalty.
